identity.name: Uzbek Khanate of Abul-Khayr

land.text: the independent eastern wing of the former Ulus of Jochi, around Tyumen and the Tura

predecessors.note: The Golden Horde row runs to 1502 on Cliopatria; its eastern wing is the White Horde / Sighnaq side.

the Tura and Tobol lands, under Ibak Khan (Sibir infobox)
the Syr Darya cities Otrar, Yasi, Arkuq and Uzgend, held by the Shaybanids c.1495

capitals.name: Tyumen (on the Tura)
capitals.note: 'consolidating nomadic groups around Tyumen and the Tura River'; the page names no capital before Sighnaq (coordinates of Tyumen as in the khanate-of-sibir dossier).

capitals.name: Sighnaq (Sunaq Ata)
capitals.note: 'The town of Sighnaq became Abu'l-Khayr's new capital' after he invaded the Syr Darya region in 1446 (coordinates as in the khanate-of-sibir and white-horde dossiers; Sighnaq is not in the gazetteer).

rulers.name: Abu'l-Khayr
rulers.note: Khan 1428-1468 (some sources have his death in 1469 or 1470); succeeded by his son Sheikh Haidar (Haider Sultan in the succession table).

correction.text: the nomadic groups 'around Tyumen and the Tura River', where Abu'l-Khayr was chosen khan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row: Cliopatria draws his realm inside its 'Khanate of Sibir' row (1429-1587), whose 1440-1481 steppe shapes the khanate-of-sibir dossier identifies as Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek steppe khanate. After a battle on the Tobol he also 'deposed and killed Kazhy Mohammed of the Khanate of Sibir' and was proclaimed Khan of Western Siberia (undated); West Siberia stays in the khanate-of-sibir dossier.

correction.text: as 1428 plus the Eastern Desht-i Kipchak: 'during the 1420s-1450s, he subordinated most of the tribal confederations of the Eastern Desht-i Kipchak and significantly expanded the borders of his state'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 1440 is Cliopatria's year for the steppe entering the Sibir shape; the page gives only the span 1420s-1450s. About 1.9 M km2 on the gazetteer for the steppe plus the Tura; no infobox area exists (Cliopatria's whole Sibir shape of 1450 is 3.9 M km2 with Siberia to the Arctic).

intersect.text: the Syr Darya and Turkestan oblasts of Kazakhstan

union.text: the Syr Darya and Turkestan lands in Kazakhstan: Qyzylorda, South Kazakhstan and Zhambyl, the part of them on the Syr Darya or inside Cliopatria's Timurid shape of 1440

correction.text: as 1440 plus the Syr Darya and Turkestan lands of Kazakhstan, where from 1446 he 'took some lands from Timurid control' and 'brought the Syr Darya and Turkestan domains of Urus Khan's descendants under his authority'; valid 1446-1449

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Oirat defeat of about 1457 and the Kazakh secession are not dated by the pages opened (the Oirats page is silent), so the shape runs to 1467; Cliopatria's Sibir shape reaches only the edge of Sighnaq (khanate-of-sibir dossier). [fx-15] Narrowed to the Kazakh part of the Syr Darya (Qyzylorda, South Kazakhstan, Zhambyl): the pages name only Sighnaq and the Turkestan domains, while the old 100 km river band ran up into Tashkent, Jizzakh, Khujand and the Fergana valley, which no page gives him (the Kazakh dossier cites the Moghulistan page for Tashkent: taken from the Timurids by Yunus Khan in 1482 or 1484). The shape now ends in 1449; the Nogai steppe leaves in the 1440s (ledger loss 1449, keyframe 1450).

union.text: the Syr Darya and Turkestan lands in Kazakhstan: Qyzylorda, South Kazakhstan and Zhambyl, the part of them on the Syr Darya or inside Cliopatria's Timurid shape of 1440

minus.text: the Nogai steppe between the Volga and the Yaik

correction.text: as 1446 without the Nogai steppe between the Volga and the Yaik: 'During the 1440s, the Manghit Yurt (Nogai Horde) separated from the Uzbek Khanate'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Kazakh Khanate page: 'During the 1440s, the Manghit Yurt (Nogai Horde) separated from the Uzbek Khanate' (decade only); the Abu'l-Khayr page names the Manghits only as 'another tribe in the White Horde' who assisted him and gives no western boundary; the Nogai Horde page has the Nogais on the lands between the Volga and the Yaik (Ural) with the capital Saraychik on the lower Yaik. The steppe west of the Kazakh line, drawn here as Cliopatria's Nogai Horde shape of 1450 (2,499 cells, 46.1-58.6E), is the Nogai dossier's from 1450; West Kazakhstan, Atyrau and the south of Aqtobe come out of the 1446 shape (1,018 cells). The Oirat defeat of about 1457 and the Kazakh secession are still not dated by any page opened, so the shape runs to 1467 (fx-15, F102).

region.text: the nomadic groups around Tyumen and the Tura River

ledger.note: 1428: Abu'l-Khayr is made khan at Tyumen. 'In 1428, Abu'l-Khayr Khan of the Shibanid dynasty became khan of the independent eastern wing of the former Ulus of Jochi' (Kazakh Khanate page); 'After his release in 1428, he consolidated nomadic groups around Tyumen and the Tura River'.

1430: the Uzbeks take Urganj. 'He attacked Khwarezm and occupied Urganj' in 1430-1431 (the span is the page's); the page does not name the owner, the timurid-empire dossier holds Khwarazm in this period.
Summer 1431: the Uzbeks leave Urganj. 'the Uzbeks could not hold the city and withdrew in summer 1431'.

region.text: the Eastern Desht-i Kipchak, the Kazakh steppe

ledger.note: c.1440: the Kazakh steppe is Abu'l-Khayr's. 'during the 1420s-1450s, he subordinated most of the tribal confederations of the Eastern Desht-i Kipchak'; the page gives the span, not a year. 1440 is the year Cliopatria's Sibir shape adds the steppe (bridging).

intersect.text: the Syr Darya and Turkestan oblasts of Kazakhstan

region.text: the Syr Darya region with Sighnaq and the Turkestan domains, in Kazakhstan

ledger.note: 1446: Abu'l-Khayr takes the Syr Darya. 'From 1446 he invaded the Syr Darya region and took some lands from Timurid control'; 'The town of Sighnaq became Abu'l-Khayr's new capital'; the Kazakh Khanate page adds the Turkestan domains of Urus Khan's descendants. [fx-15: region narrowed from the 100 km Syr Darya band to the Kazakh oblasts (Qyzylorda, South Kazakhstan, Zhambyl): the pages name Sighnaq and Turkestan only, and the timurid-empire keyframes of 1447-1468 now leave exactly these oblasts out. Tashkent, Jizzakh, Khujand and the Fergana valley stay Timurid (Tashkent to Yunus Khan 1482-84, Moghulistan page).]
1446: the capital moves to Sighnaq. 'The town of Sighnaq became Abu'l-Khayr's new capital'.

region.text: the Nogai steppe between the Volga and the Yaik

ledger.note: 1440s: the Manghit Yurt separates. 'During the 1440s, the Manghit Yurt (Nogai Horde) separated from the Uzbek Khanate' (Kazakh Khanate page, decade only; the Abu'l-Khayr page calls the Manghits 'another tribe in the White Horde' who helped him, with no frontier). 1449 is the last year of the decade and the year before the nogai-horde dossier starts (1450, Cliopatria's shape), so the Volga-Yaik steppe leaves the khanate here and the Nogai found takes it as nobody's land (fx-15, F102).

c.1468: the Kazakh tribes leave. Kerei and Janibek 'rejected Abu'l-Khayr's authority and migrated to Moghulistan' (no date); 'Around 1470, the Kazakh tribes, led by Janibek and Kerei, settled in what is now Kazakhstan'; Kazakh historiography dates the khanate to 1465, Russian to 1470-71. 1468 is Abu'l-Khayr's death year (Abu'l-Khayr page), a bridging date.

region.text: the steppe, the Syr Darya and the Tura

ledger.note: 1468: Abu'l-Khayr dies and his khanate breaks up. 'He died in 1468, though some sources say 1469 or 1470'; Sheikh Haidar succeeded him. His grandson Muhammad Shaybani 'later unified the Uzbeks in the early 16th century'; about 1495-96 the Kazakhs and Shaybanids divided the Syr Darya cities (Kazakh Khanate page).

wars.name: Abu’l-Khayr’s Khwarezm campaigns
wars.outcome: Urganj was occupied in 1430-31 but could not be held and was abandoned in summer 1431; Uzbek armies attacked Khwarezm again in 1435-36 without lasting gain.

wars.name: Uzbek conquest of the Syr Darya

zones.text: the Syr Darya region with Sighnaq

wars.outcome: From 1446 Abu'l-Khayr took lands on the Syr Darya from Timurid control and made Sighnaq his capital; in 1451 he marched with Abu Sa'id on Samarkand, where Abdullah was defeated and killed, and was paid off outside the gates.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; the pages give no boundary for any phase.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row for Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek Khanate: its 'Khanate of Sibir' row (1429-1587) draws his steppe in the same colour, and the khanate-of-sibir dossier (ia-02-c) keeps those shapes as 'ok' while saying the Uzbek khanate belongs to this additions batch. This dossier is that khanate; the rendering agents should draw the steppe and Syr Darya of 1440-1467 in this dossier's colour and keep West Siberia in the Sibir colour (both dossiers have Abu'l-Khayr as khan of Sibir 1428-1468, per the Abu'l-Khayr infobox).

Thin points: the 1457 defeat by the Oirats and the secession of Kerei and Janibek are not dated by any page opened (the Oirats page is silent, the Abu'l-Khayr page does not mention them, the Kazakh Khanate page gives no dates for the migration); the Syr Darya towns other than Sighnaq are not placed; the year of the steppe subordination is a span (1420s-1450s); the owner of Urganj in 1430 is not named. His death is 1468 (Abu'l-Khayr page), 1469 or 1470 in some sources, and Russian historiography dates the Kazakh Khanate to his death (1470-71). The 'shaybanids' successor refers to the Cliopatria row Shaybanids 1497-1511 (ia-03), whose first shape is Muhammad Shaybani's Transoxiana.

Gazetteer names: Sighnaq (Sunaq Ata) is not a place in the gazetteer; capital coordinates only.
